question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $3$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}-3 & =-\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{x}{2}-3+3 & =-\frac{1}{3}+3 \\ \frac{x}{2}+0 & =-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{9}{3} \\ \frac{x}{2} & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, multiplying both sides of the equation by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =\frac{8}{3} \\ \cancel{2}\cdot \frac{x}{\cancel{2}} & =2\cdot \frac{8}{3} \\ x & =\frac{16}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
